What to Consider When Buying a Laptop

The following are ten key factors you should consider when buying a laptop in Kenya. 

1. Purpose and Usage

The first question you should ask yourself is, what am I going to use this laptop?  Is it for basic tasks such as typing and browsing the internet, or advanced tasks such as gaming, professional work, or multimedia consumption? Don't just go for any laptop; maybe it's because of the price. 

2. Processor (CPU)

Since you have determined your purpose, it's time you choose a powerful processor that suits your needs. rememebr,  The more updated and powerful  your processor, the faster your laptop can complete its tasks. I would prefer you to choose Intel Core i5 or later and AMD Ryzen 5 or or later due to their performance and efficiency.

3. RAM

Your computer RAM will determine the amount of tasks you can carry on your laptop simultaneously. More RAM ensures smoother multitasking. I recommend you go for a minimum of 8GB, or 4GB but not less. Choose 16GB or more if you have demanding tasks such as graphic design,  video editing, or gaming. 

4. Storage

How much space do you need? 

We have two types of storage: HDDs and SSDs. HDDs offer more storage capacity at a lower cost. However, A laptop with SSDs is faster and more reliable. Sometimes I prefer you go for 256GB SSD than Going for 500GB HDD. 

5. Graphics Card (GPU)

A graphic card of your computer is very important especially if you are planning to use your computer for gaming, video editing, and graphic design. If this is the case, then I recommend you choose a laptop with integrated graphics that are sufficient for everyday tasks. For gaming, for instance, you will need a laptop with MSI Gaming AMD Radeon RX 6600. 

6. Battery Life

Your laptop battery should last at least 3 hours when not connected to power. This means that you should look for laptops with long battery life if you plan to use your laptop on the go frequently.

7. Display Quality

This also goes back to the purpose of the laptop you are about to buy. You should consider the screen size, resolution, and panel type. The standard quality I recommend is 14", 1920×1080, and LCD screens.

8. Build Quality and Design

A durable and well-designed laptop can withstand daily wear and tear. Consider the laptop's weight and portability as well.

9. Connectivity Options

Ensure the laptop has sufficient ports (USB, HDMI, etc.) and connectivity features (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth) to meet your needs.

10. Budget

Your budget is very important when you are looking for a laptop. Although there is no specific budget for a laptop, you will get the best laptop (refurbished) if your budget is between Ksh 20,000 and Ksh 40,000. However, with less than Ksh 20,000 you can also get one but not powerful for tasks such as video editing, graphic design, and computer programming. Remember to balance cost with features and performance.

Difference between Toners and Cartridges

Before diving into the best deals, let's clarify the difference between toners and cartridges and their significance in the printing process:
  • Toner: Toners are used in laser printers. A toner is a fine powder that creates text and images on paper through a heat process.
  • Cartridge: Cartridges are used in inkjet printers. They contain liquid ink that is sprayed onto the paper to form text and images.
Ink cartridges are always more affordable than toner, however, they last less and need to be replaced more frequently. However, the choice between a toner or cartridge solely depends on the printer model and the quality of prints you require.

Factors to Consider When Buying Toners and Cartridges

When purchasing toners and cartridges, consider the following factors to ensure you get the best quality and value:
  1. Compatibility: Ensure the toner or cartridge is compatible with your printer model.
  2. Yield: Check the number of pages the toner or cartridge can print. If your pocket allows, go for higher yield options since they are cost-effective for high-volume printing.
  3. Quality: Look for products that deliver sharp, clear prints without smudging or streaking.
  4. Brand: If you are not sure which type to buy, ensure you opt for reputable brands to ensure reliability and performance.

Title: 4 Tips to Reduce Printing & Other Stationery Expenses
Content:
Introduction Stationery and office supplies are important components for daily business operations. However, if their costs, are not carefully monitored, they can make a business lose a lot of cash annually. In an article published by Chron in 2019, it is estimated that, in the US:
  • Businesses with 1 to 4 employees spend about $77 to $92 per employee monthly on stationery and office consumables like printing paper, pens, printer, toners etc.
  • Those with about 40 employees spend between $45-$53 per employee per month.
  • Those with over 200 employees spend $27-$32 per employee per month.
These figures are just an average as the costs will vary depending on their nature of work and the cost of stationery and office supplies in the region they are located. However, it paints a picture of the cost implication of stationery and office supplies in an organisation. Having worked in the accounts department of several organisations and currently being in the business of stationery supplies, I have learnt a lot about how businesses can reduce their stationery & office supplies costs. Here are 4 of the tips that a business can apply to reduce their stationery and office supply costs.
  1. Re-using used printing paper
Printing or photocopy paper is a major office consumable. It is also prone to wastage which increases the overall stationery expenses. A simple solution like reusing printing paper can go a long way in reducing this cost. I would encourage the use of double sided printing for all documents. But, if a document has been printed on one side and has already fulfilled its purpose, it can be used for printing on the other side as long as it does not contain sensitive data that should not be shared. These printouts can be used internally for meetings or other uses instead of using new sheets of paper.
  1. Go Digital
By leveraging on technology, a business can save a lot in terms of stationery costs, especially printing paper, toners and inks.  This can be done by encouraging the use of saving and sharing documents online. Limit hardcopy printing to only those document that require to be printed. Google Drive is a free web based cloud solutions which allows you to store and access documents anywhere. It can be used by small firms and individuals as they move towards digitalizing their operations. Larger organisations can laisse with their IT Consultants to find the best way to go digital in their organisations.
  • Having a centralised procurement department
For large organizations with many branches or departments, they can consider having a central procurement office where all procurement and purchases are done. This will help in negotiating for better terms due to bulk buying. With such a department, all requests and issuance of stationery to other departments or branches can be done at one point. This will reduce wastage and encourage sharing of resources like printers and other business machines and thus reducing costs. It will also help in planning for purchases and managing the available resources.  
  1. Using the right printers for your organisation and adopting the use of compatible toners
A wrong printer can lead to losing lots of money through printing costs. For example; for a small organization with minimal printing needs, I would recommend the use of inkjet printers instead of smaller desk jet printers as liquid printer ink is way cheaper and has higher yield than cartridges used in digital printers. For larger organisations with more printing and photocopying requirements, they can consider using a commercial printer that is centrally placed instead of having several small printers for different offices or departments. Though the initial costs to acquire these printers may seem high, it will save the business a lot of money in the long run. In terms of consumables like toners and printer ink, using compatible ones can reduce printing costs by up to 50%. Compatible toners and inks are those made by third party companies under licence by the OEM. Unlike the the Original OEM toners, the compatible ones can be made from recycled materials which makes them cheaper and also environmentally friendly. At Finamax Business Solutions Ltd, we advise our clients on the right compatible toners to use depending on their machines. I have done a separate, more detailed article on the differences of compatible and original toners and their benefits. Conclusion These 4 tips are just a few of the methods that a business can apply to reduce printing costs. Different organisations may have different methods that will apply to them based on their nature of operations. However, for most organizations, applying these tips can help them reduce printing costs significantly. At Finamax, we are always ready to advise on ways on matters of stationery and office supplies. Feel free to reach out to us for more information or advise.
